title: San Francisco Bay Expeditions
subtitle: Sea and land, 1542-1776, after the Mission Dolores exhibit panel
abstract: The exploration of the San Francisco-Monterey coast as the exhibit panel presents it: five sea approaches and the land expeditions of 1769-1776. Every course here is INTERPRETIVE: a generalized line meaning 'they passed roughly this way,' traced after the exhibit panel and the published diary reconstructions (Crespi ed. Brown; Font; Palou; Bolton's Anza volumes), never a surveyed track. Diary citations sit on the key stops; C-A record anchors get attached in a later review pass, not invented here. C-A anchors attached 2026-10-16 from a catalog sweep (Docs plainly concerning each expedition per our own catalog); they are catalog-level matches, leaf review pending.
legend_note: All courses generalized and interpretive, after the Mission Dolores exhibit panel and the published diaries.

routes.label: Cabrillo & Ferrelo, 1542-43

stops.name: Cabrillo passes this coast northbound
stops.summary: The first European ships along this shore, standing well out; no landing on this stretch. Ferrelo repassed in 1543. Course generalized (interpretive).

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Cabrillo relation (Wagner, Spanish Voyages to the Northwest Coast).
Predates the provincial archive; published sources only (see the stop).

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Cabrillo relation (Wagner, Spanish Voyages to the Northwest Coast).

routes.label: Manila galleons, 1565-1815

stops.name: The Manila ships' landfall run
stops.summary: Returning galleons made their American landfall to the north and ran south along this coast for Acapulco, year after year for two and a half centuries. Course generalized (interpretive).

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Schurz, The Manila Galleon.
The standing anticontraband regime for receiving the Manila ship at San José del Cabo: C-A 1 Doc 8 (Neve, 24 Oct 1775)

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Schurz, The Manila Galleon; the Nao regime in C-A 1 Doc 8.

routes.label: Drake, 1579

stops.name: Drake careens in a 'faire and good Baye'
stops.summary: Five weeks ashore among the Coast Miwok. The landing site is a famous fight; Drakes Bay is the prevailing identification and the one the exhibit panel follows.
stops.notes: Site identification debated; shown at Drakes Bay per the panel.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; The World Encompassed (1628); cf. the site controversy literature.
Predates the provincial archive; published sources only (see the stop).

ends.label: up from the Spanish coast, prizes aboard

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; The World Encompassed (1628); landing-site identification debated.

routes.label: Cermeno, 1595

stops.name: The San Agustin wrecks under Cermeno
stops.summary: The Manila ship sent to survey the coast anchored in the bay behind Point Reyes and was driven ashore; the crew ran south in an open launch, surveying as they went. Her porcelain cargo still washes into Coast Miwok sites.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Wagner, 'The Voyage of Cermeno' (CHS Quarterly, 1924).
Predates the provincial archive; published sources only (see the stop).

ends.label: south to Acapulco, surveying from the launch

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Wagner, 'The Voyage of Cermeno' (CHS Quarterly, 1924).

routes.label: Ayala & Canizares, 1775

stops.name: The San Carlos inside the Golden Gate
stops.summary: Ayala brings the first ship through the Gate by night and anchors off the island he names for Our Lady of the Angels; forty-four days inside the bay while Canizares surveys it by longboat.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Galvin ed., The First Spanish Entry into San Francisco Bay, 1775.
A corporal and nine soldiers assigned to navy lieutenant Juan Manuel de Ayala at San Francisco: C-A 1 Doc 74 (20 Jan 1776)
The pilot Cañizares elsewhere in the record, commanding the supply packet in 1774: C-A 1 Doc 109

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Galvin ed., The First Spanish Entry into San Francisco Bay, 1775; C-A 1 Docs 74, 109.

routes.citation: Longboat survey arm, interpretive; Canizares's 1775 plano and Galvin ed. (1971).

routes.citation: Longboat survey arm, interpretive; Canizares's 1775 plano and Galvin ed. (1971).

routes.label: Portola-Crespi-Rivera-Serra, 1769

stops.name: The bay discovered from Sweeney Ridge
stops.summary: Ortega's scouts, hunting Monterey, stumble instead onto 'a great arm of the sea': the first European sight of San Francisco Bay. The whole strategic geography of Alta California changes in an afternoon.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Crespi diary, ed. Brown, A Description of Distant Roads.

stops.name: The turning-point camp on San Francisquito Creek
stops.summary: The expedition's council under the tall redwood (the palo alto): short of food, they turn back south for San Diego.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Crespi diary, ed. Brown.
Gálvez's 14-article sailing instruction for the San Carlos, the sea half of the Sacred Expedition: C-A 1 Doc 14 (5 Jan 1769)
Gálvez's companion military instruction to Fages: C-A 1 Doc 15
Rivera's first land division, Velicatá to San Diego, the 1769 diary copied verbatim in the archive: C-A 62 Doc 20

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Crespi diary ed. Brown, A Description of Distant Roads; C-A 1 Docs 14-15, C-A 62 Doc 20.

routes.label: Portola-Fages-Crespi, 1770

stops.name: Monterey occupied; the coast re-walked
stops.summary: With Monterey finally recognized and occupied, the 1769 trail up the coast is re-run to probe the new bay.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Crespi diary, ed. Brown.
Viceroy Croix's measures to establish the Presidio of Monterey and the missions, acknowledging Fages's reports: C-A 1 Doc 23 (12 Nov 1770)

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Crespi diary ed. Brown; C-A 1 Doc 23.

routes.label: Fages-Crespi, 1772

stops.name: First Europeans at the Carquinez strait
stops.summary: Marching up the eastern bayshore, Fages and Crespi reach the narrows where the whole interior drains to the sea, and look across at the mouths of the great rivers.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Crespi diary, ed. Brown.

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Crespi diary ed. Brown (30 Mar 1772 at the Carquinez strait).

routes.label: Rivera, 1774
routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Palou (Bolton, Historical Memoirs of New California).

routes.label: Rivera-Palou, 1774

stops.name: Palou's cross at Point Lobos
stops.summary: Rivera and Palou walk the peninsula to its tip and plant a cross above the Gate: the marker Ayala's men will find standing the next summer.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Palou diary (Bolton, Historical Memoirs of New California).
Bucareli acknowledges the DIARY of Rivera's Nov 1774 reconnaissance of the port of San Francisco in company with Fr. Palóu: C-A 1 Doc 63 (24 May 1775)
The resolution to occupy the port of San Francisco with two missions: C-A 1 Doc 58 (2 Jan 1775)
The 1773 oficio anticipating Anza's coming and the reconnaissance of the port: C-A 14 Doc 395

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Palou diary (Bolton); C-A 1 Docs 58, 63; C-A 14 Doc 395.

routes.label: Anza-Font, 1774

stops.name: Anza's first overland party reaches Monterey
stops.summary: The Sonora road proved: Alta California can be reached, and colonized, overland.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Bolton, Anza's California Expeditions.
Bucareli authorizes Anza to open the overland road via the Colorado and Gila: C-A 1 Doc 42 (19 Sep 1773)
The same order as Savage calendars it: C-A 14 Doc 396

ends.label: from Tubac, Sonora, via the Colorado

routes.citation: Course interpretive, after the exhibit panel; Bolton, Anza's California Expeditions; C-A 1 Doc 42, C-A 14 Doc 396.

routes.label: Anza-Font, 1776

stops.name: The presidio site chosen at the Gate
stops.summary: Font: a table-land commanding the narrows, 'the harbor of harbors.' The white cliff above the Gate becomes the presidio of San Francisco that autumn.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Font's complete diary (Bolton, Anza's California Expeditions IV).

stops.name: The arroyo de los Dolores chosen for the mission
stops.summary: The sheltered creek and lagoon two leagues in from the Gate, named for the Friday of Sorrows: the site of Mission San Francisco de Asis, where these exhibit panels hang today.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Font's complete diary (Bolton IV).

stops.name: To the mouths of the rivers
stops.summary: Anza and Font round the southern bay, run the eastern shore past the strait, and look into the delta before turning for home: the whole future mission-and-presidio geography seen in one circuit.

sources.citation: After the exhibit panel; Font's complete diary (Bolton IV).
Viceregal instruction warning Rivera of Anza's coming WITH FAMILIES to occupy the port of San Francisco: C-A 14 Doc 400 (15 Dec 1774)
Anza's mule trains and logistics franked to the expedition: C-A 1 Doc 62 (10 Jan 1775)
Port reconnaissance and artillery to proceed at Anza's arrival: C-A 1 Doc 75 (20 Jan 1776)
Rivera orders Lt. José Moraga to take charge of the expedition on Anza's withdrawal: C-A 14 Doc 432 (4 Feb 1776)

ends.label: from Tubac with the colonist families
back to Monterey; Moraga leads the settlers on to found San Francisco, Jun 1776
